source_text: Εἰ δέ τινα ὑπέλθοι καὶ ἡ ἔννοια αὕτη ὅτι, εἰ θεὸν ὡμολογοῦμεν βοηθόν, οὐκ ἄν, ὡς λέγομεν, ὑπὸ ἀδίκων ἐκρατούμεθα καὶ ἐτιμωρούμεθα, καὶ τοῦτο διαλύσω. Ὁ θεὸς τὸν πάντα κόσμον ποιήσας καὶ τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀνθρώποις ὑποτάξας καὶ τὰ οὐράνια στοιχεῖα εἰς αὔξησιν καρπῶν καὶ ὡρῶν μεταβολὰς κοσμήσας καὶ θεῖον τούτοις νόμον τάξας, ἃ καὶ αὐτὰ δι᾿ ἀνθρώπους φαίνεται πεποιηκώς, τὴν μὲν τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ τῶν ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν πρόνοιαν ἀγγέλοις, οὓς ἐπὶ τούτοις ἔταξε, παρέδωκεν. Οἱ δ᾿ ἄγγελοι, παραβάντες τήνδε τὴν τάξιν, γυναικῶν μίξεσιν ἡττήθησαν καὶ παῖδας ἐτέκνωσαν, οἵ εἰσιν οἱ λεγόμενοι δαίμονες. Καὶ προσέτι λοιπὸν τὸ ἀνθρώπειον γένος ἑαυτοῖς ἐδούλωσαν· τὰ μὲν διὰ μαγικῶν γραφῶν, τὰ δὲ διὰ φόβων καὶ τιμωριῶν, ὧν ἐπέφερον, τὸ δὲ διὰ διδαχῆς θυμάτων καὶ θυμιαμάτων καὶ σπονδῶν, ὧν ἐνδεεῖς γεγόνασι μετὰ τὸ πάθεσιν ἐπιθυμιῶν δουλωθῆναι· καὶ εἰς ἀνθρώπους φόνους, πολέμους, μοιχείας, ἀπολασίας καὶ πᾶσαν κακίαν ἔσπειραν. Ὅθεν καὶ ποιηταὶ καὶ μυθολόγοι, ἀγνοοῦντες τοὺς ἀγγέλους καὶ τοὺς ἐξ αὐτῶν γεννηθέντας δαίμονας ταῦτα πρᾶξαι εἰς ἄῤῥενας καὶ θηλείας καὶ πόλεις καὶ ἔθνη, ἅπερ συνέγραψαν, εἰς αὐτὸν τὸν θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ὡς ἀπ᾿ αὐτοῦ σπορᾷ γενομένους υἱοὺς καὶ τῶν λεχθέντων ἐκείνου ἀδελφῶν καὶ τέκνων ὁμοίως τῶν ἀπ᾿ ἐκείνων, Ποσειδῶνος καὶ Πλούτωνος, ἀνήνεγκαν. Ὀνόματι γὰρ ἕκαστον, ὅπερ ἕκαστος ἑαυτῷ τῶν ἀγγέλων καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις ἔθετο, προσηγόρευσαν.
thought_title: Why God lets Christians suffer: the fallen angels and demons
orientation: Justin is answering an imagined objection that if God were truly the Christians' helper, they would not be overpowered and punished by unjust men.
pass_a_gloss: But if this thought also should come upon someone, that, if we confessed God [as] helper, we would not, as we say, be overpowered by unjust [men] and be punished, this too I will dissolve. God, having made the whole world and having subjected the earthly things to humans and having adorned the heavenly elements for increase of fruits and changes of seasons and having appointed a divine law for these things, which things also themselves for the sake of humans he appears to have made, the care of humans and of the things under heaven he handed over to angels, whom he appointed over these things. But the angels, having transgressed this order, were overcome by intercourse with women and begot children, who are the ones called demons. And in addition thereafter they enslaved the human race to themselves; partly through magical writings, partly through fears and punishments which they brought upon [them], partly through teaching of sacrifices and incense and libations, of which they became in need after they were enslaved to passions of desires; and into humans they sowed murders, wars, adulteries, excesses, and every evil. Whence also poets and mythologists, not knowing that the angels and the demons begotten from them did these things against males and females and cities and nations, which things they wrote down, attributed [them] to God himself and to the sons begotten as from him by seed and to the brothers of those spoken of by him and likewise to the children of those from them, Poseidon and Pluto. For by the name which each of the angels set for himself and for his children, they addressed each one.

choices.why: The verb means to creep in or steal upon; 'come upon' preserves the sense of a thought arising unexpectedly in someone's mind.
Justin uses a forensic metaphor of dissolving an objection; 'dissolve' keeps the image of breaking down an argument.
The passive of ἡττάομαι means to be defeated or worsted; 'were overcome' fits the context of being conquered by desire for intercourse.
The noun means enjoyment or indulgence, often with a negative sense of self-indulgence; 'excesses' captures the moral failing Justin lists among vices.
The verb means to carry up or refer back; here it means the poets referred these deeds upward to God and his supposed sons, so 'attributed' is the clearest rendering.

pass_b_english: But someone may also raise this objection: if we confess God as our helper, why, as we say, are we overpowered and punished by unjust men? I will dissolve this objection too.

God made the whole world. He subjected earthly things to human beings. He adorned the heavenly elements to bring about the growth of fruits and the changes of seasons, and he appointed a divine law for them. All of this he clearly made for the sake of human beings. He then handed over the care of human beings and of everything under heaven to angels, whom he appointed for this task.

But the angels transgressed this order. They were overcome by intercourse with women and begot children, and these are the ones called demons. And after that, they enslaved the human race to themselves. They did this partly through books of magic, partly through the fears and punishments they inflicted, and partly through teaching about sacrifices, incense, and libations. These were things the demons themselves came to need once they had been enslaved to the passions of their desires. Into human beings they sowed murders, wars, adulteries, excesses, and every kind of evil.

This is why the poets and mythologists, not knowing that it was the angels and the demons born from them who did these things against males and females, cities and nations, attributed the deeds they wrote about to God himself and to his sons, to the brothers of those sons, and to their children, such as the gods Poseidon and Pluto. For they called each one by whatever name each angel had given to himself and to his children.

problems.why: English treats Poseidon and Pluto as examples of brothers/children, but Greek names them as examples of the 'sons' themselves (the angels/demons).
problems.ruling: Ποσειδῶνος καὶ Πλούτωνος are genitives dependent on ἀδελφῶν καὶ τέκνων, not the υἱούς; English apposition misidentifies them as sons.
